title: Finite-presentation closed envelope without a separation condition
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme, and quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact; a morphism is quasi-compact when its pullback by any affine scheme has quasi-compact source. A morphism is quasi-separated when its diagonal is quasi-compact. A closed immersion is representable and is a closed immersion on every scheme test [def-weil-closed-immersion]; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Local finite type and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type. Finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation. Let $X$ and $Y$ be quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces and let $f:X\to Y$ be locally of finite type. There exist an algebraic space $W$, a closed immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow W$, and a morphism of finite presentation $h:W\to Y$ with $h\circ j=f$. No separatedness is asserted for $h$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-absolute-noetherian-approximation] to $X$: write $X=\varprojlim_i X_i$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, indexed by a small nonempty directed set, with affine transitions and $X_i$ quasi-separated and of finite type over $\mathbf Z$. The scheme $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is locally Noetherian since each ideal of $\mathbf Z$ is generated by its least positive element (or is zero). On an etale scheme atlas $U_i\to X_i$, the map $U_i\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is locally of finite type. The scheme theorem [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] makes it locally of finite presentation. The etale-chart definition gives local finite presentation of $X_i\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$; finite type supplies quasi-compactness and absolute quasi-separatedness supplies its quasi-separatedness, hence finite presentation (the chart argument of 06G4). Set $Z_i=X_i\times Y$ and $p_i:Z_i\to Y$. Base change preserves finite presentation by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], so $p_i$ is finitely presented. Each $X_i$ is quasi-compact by finite type; [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products] makes $Z_i$ qcqs.

proof.text: The fibre products are categorical by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Their universal property identifies $\varprojlim_i Z_i$ over $Y$ with $X\times Y$: a compatible cone $T\to Z_i$ over $Y$ is exactly its fixed map $T\to Y$ together with a compatible cone $T\to X_i$, hence a unique map $T\to X$. Every transition $Z_j\to Z_i$ is a base change of the affine transition $X_j\to X_i$, hence affine by its affine-scheme test. The graph $\gamma=(1_X,f):X\to X\times Y$ is a monomorphism since its first projection is $1_X$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-eventual-monomorphism] with base $B=Y$, source $A=X$ and system $(Z_i)$: $X$ is quasi-compact, $X\to Y$ is locally of finite type, and every $Z_i$ is quasi-separated. Choose $i$ such that $u=(\pi_i,f):X\to Z_i$ is monic.

The composite $p_i u=f$ is locally of finite type, so [lem-sfb-space-lft-cancellation] makes $u$ locally of finite type. Both $X$ and $Z_i$ are qcqs. Thus [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-lft-mono-quasiaffine] makes $u$ quasi-affine. Apply [lem-sfb-space-quasiaffine-fp-envelope] to $u$ and its qcqs target $Z_i$: obtain $j:X\hookrightarrow W$ closed and $v:W\to Z_i$ finitely presented with $vj=u$. Put $h=p_i v$. By [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition], $h$ is finitely presented. Finally $hj=p_i vj=p_i u=f$. This proves precisely the required envelope without claiming separatedness.
